name: lightweight tag versus signed target-commit scope split

PROVIDER_VERIFIED_ANNOTATED_TAG.reason: tag ref points directly to a commit; there is no annotated tag object whose tag signature can be provider-verified

PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT.reason: the exact target commit itself is immutable and GitHub reports verified=true/reason=valid
PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT.scope: source-state/authorship identity of the exact commit under GitHub-provider trust, not cryptographic authentication of the release tag name as a separately signed object

counterfactual_controls.case: treat lightweight tag name as equivalent to signed annotated tag
ignore exact target commit SHA and retain only release page/tag name
use exact verified target commit under commit-origin rule

result.transversal_value: The origin lattice distinguishes release-intent authentication from source-state authentication. A lightweight tag can point at a separately signed commit, so scheduled Chat may trust the exact commit as provider-verified source state while refusing to call the tag itself signed/authenticated.
limits: Does not authenticate the lightweight tag name as a separately signed object.
Does not make the release object immutable.
Does not verify release assets or perform fresh signing.

frontier: Formalize choice/precedence table for exact commit, signed annotated tag, lightweight tag->verified commit, own repository identity and unsigned/mutable references.
Test signed-tag target commit that is unverified if one is found; signed tag should still authenticate target object identity while commit-level signer semantics remain separate.
Use origin classification before any content semantic parser or proof rule.
